_comment: Packages whose own tests provision real ephemeral infrastructure (Docker containers via testcontainers-go, or multi-process real-time distributed coordination), so a test failure inside one of them is, per FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61, at least as likely to be local resource contention as a real defect: 'the specific package that loses the race changes between runs... is the signature of resource contention, not a code defect.' tools/testgate (the local pre-push gate; see .githooks/pre-push and the Makefile's push-gate target) downgrades a test failure confined to a package listed here to a warning rather than blocking the push. GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) is unaffected because it runs no tests at all: it runs `make ci-remote` (build, vet, fmt, tidy, the two pinned scanners, the docs and chart checks), so nothing in this file changes what that workflow accepts. What it does change is the local run, and the local run is now the only place a test result comes from at all: `make ci` still uses the bare, non-tolerant test-race/test-integration targets and hard-fails on a listed package exactly like an unlisted one, while `make push-gate` downgrades it to a warning. An entry added here without a real, written reason is therefore a package that nothing anywhere checks. Every entry names one package by its full import path and a reason grepped/derived from real evidence (a specific test, a specific failure shape, or CLAUDE.md's own list of Docker-dependent packages), never a directory glob or 'seems container-ish' guess. A package that stops provisioning real infrastructure should be removed from this list in the same change that removes the infrastructure, the same staleness discipline gosec-waivers.json's own header asks for.

packages.reason: FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestGrandIntegration specifically as a repeat offender under full parallel `-race` load. Confirmed again in the AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-12/13): TestGrandIntegration_EachKindReachesItsOwnAdapter hung 913s behind a device-lock-contention redelivery loop, and a later run failed a different test, TestGrandIntegration, on a NATS container port-mapping race ('port "4222/tcp" not found'). Both reproduced as clean, fast passes every time when rerun in isolation, and a git-stash baseline comparison proved the first failure was not reachable from that session's own diff at all.

FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestNatsBus_SurvivesConnectionSeverance and TestNatsBusPublish_DistinctEventsBothStored as failing under full-suite parallel load and passing individually every time. Dials a real, ephemeral NATS container per CLAUDE.md's own list of Docker-dependent packages.

FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestNewNatsLockManagerRejectsOldServer as failing under full-suite parallel load and passing individually every time. Starts up to seven real containers in a single package (the Makefile's own GO_TEST_TIMEOUT comment), the heaviest real-infrastructure user in the module.

CLAUDE.md's own list of packages that dial real ephemeral Docker containers (NATS, sshd) names this one alongside internal/lock and internal/event; genuinely container-dependent by the identical mechanism, and excluding it while including its two named siblings would be an arbitrary distinction. OBSERVED DIRECTLY 2026-08-16, which is the correction that matters: this entry used to say 'not yet observed to flake directly', and it was admitted on the strength of the mechanism alone. It has now been seen in two consecutive full `make ci` runs, with the same signature both times, `failed to get mapped port: port "2222/tcp" not found` raised by TestSSHContainer_StoppedContainerRetriesThenBreakerOpens and by the shared-container setup TestSSHContainer_ExecSuccess and its three siblings use. The mechanism is precise rather than general: the openssh-server container starts, satisfies its wait.ForLog("done.") strategy, and has lost its published port binding by the time the very next statement asks for it, which is what a container that has exited looks like to an inspect. Under full parallel -race load that test took 18.31s; run alone immediately afterwards, against the same daemon and the same image, it passed in 9.35s. The goleak failures that accompany it in the same runs are downstream rather than separate: a setup that t.Fatal's skips the terminate that would stop the testcontainers reaper, so the leaked goroutine is a consequence of the port failure and not an independent defect.

AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-12): TestAgent_FailedExecutionEventuallyDeadLetters and TestAgent_ReleaseGate_PullsFiveDispatchesWithoutDuplicating both failed under full-suite parallel load on a real NATS container port-mapping race ('connection string: port "4222/tcp" not found'), each confirmed passing individually afterward.

AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-12): TestCLI_RunExecutesSSHTransport failed under full-suite parallel load ('failed to get mapped port: port "2222/tcp" not found', a real ephemeral sshd container's own port-mapping race), confirmed passing individually afterward.

AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-13): TestControllerLeaderElection_ReleaseGate reported 'SPLIT BRAIN DETECTED' under full-suite parallel load, a real multi-replica timing race against a real NATS-backed lease, confirmed passing individually afterward. Real-container tests generally (see internal/adapters/legacy's own Release Gate, run from this package's test binary indirectly through tests/e2e, and this package's own leader-election gate) live here.

AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-13): TestLeaderElection_ThreeReplicas_OnlyOneLeaderAndGracefulHandover failed under full-suite parallel load (a real three-replica timing race against a real NATS-backed lease, the same mechanism cmd/controller's own leader-election gate exercises one layer up), confirmed passing individually afterward.

Real Docker container tests (the Ansible and native adapter Release Gates, internal/adapters/legacy.DockerOrchestrator and the SSH mesh's own ephemeral sshd containers) run from this package's own test binary; structurally identical in kind to cmd/pleiades and internal/runner above, both of which have flaked. OBSERVED DIRECTLY 2026-08-16, on the same day and for the same reason as internal/transport/ssh's entry above: this one used to say 'not yet observed to flake in a full-suite run', and TestSSHMeshReleaseGate_RealSecretThroughTheFullChain then failed under a full `make push-gate` and passed on a rerun. Both entries were admitted on mechanism alone and both were right about the mechanism, which is the argument for prophylactic listing and also the reason a 'not yet observed' clause has to be revisited rather than left to age into an unexamined fact: a reader six months from now cannot tell a prediction from a record, and the whole value of this file is that every entry is a record.

internal/adapters/legacy/docker_orchestrator_test.go and its own release-gate-style tests provision real ephemeral Docker containers directly (testcontainers-go), the same mechanism cmd/runner's Ansible Release Gate composes one layer up.
internal/topology/stream_container_test.go provisions a real ephemeral NATS/JetStream container directly (testcontainers-go) to prove stream/consumer configuration against a real server, not a fake.
internal/ent/conformance_backends_test.go provisions a real ephemeral Postgres container directly (testcontainers-go) to run the same conformance suite against both SQLite and Postgres backends.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`'s test-repeat: TestReleaseGate_AnExpiringCredentialEvictsALiveConnection failed with 'container port: port "4222/tcp" not found', the identical NATS container port-mapping race this file's own tests/e2e entry already records by name. Not a defect in the test: the failure is inside the shared broker-start helper before any assertion runs. Reran the package alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 26.9s, which is the isolation signature FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 describes. The package provisions two real ephemeral nats:2.14.4-alpine containers, one per Release Gate, and both run a JetStream-enabled broker in operator mode, so it belongs on this list for the same mechanism as internal/event and internal/lock.

Observed 2026-08-26 in the same push-gate run as internal/meshid above: TestReleaseGate_AnInputResolvesOutOfARealVault failed with 'container port: port "8200/tcp" not found'. Same race, different image: the port mapping is not published yet when the test reads it, under full parallel repeat load. Reran alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 12.9s. The package provisions a real ephemeral HashiCorp Vault container. That two different packages lost the same race in one run, on two different ports, is itself FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61's stated signature: 'the specific package that loses the race changes between runs'.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`'s test-repeat: TestConformance_LeavesNoGoroutinesBehind failed with 'found unexpected goroutines', and the goroutine it named was testcontainers' OWN reaper connection (testcontainers-go@v0.43.0/reaper.go:544-549), not anything pkg/netconf starts. The reaper connects lazily and its goroutine can still be live when a later package's goleak check runs, so whether this fires depends on which package happens to be last to touch the shared reaper. Reran the test alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 12.6s. The package provisions a real ephemeral netopeer2 NETCONF container, which is the same criterion every other entry here meets. This is a leak-detector reporting a dependency's own goroutine, not a leak in this repository's code, so it is listed rather than chased.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`, and the evidence is unusually clean because the package PASSED TWICE in the same run before failing: ok at test-race and ok at test-repeat, then FAIL inside push-gate-coverage, which is the fourth full suite pass of one invocation. Same commit, same code, same machine. The four tests named were TestConnect_Succeeds, TestConnect_UnreachableEndpoint, TestDiscover_YieldsAccountThenInstances and TestSync_RoundTripsRealInstances, and the failure is not in any of them: it is 'shared LocalStack container setup failed: ... wait until ready: get state: Get http://%2Fvar%2Frun%2Fdocker.sock/... context deadline exceeded', which is the Docker daemon failing to answer a state query, not an assertion. The package provisions a real ephemeral LocalStack container, the heaviest single container this repository starts, so it is the first to lose when the daemon is saturated late in a multi-pass run.
